# pintr

> pintr generates images with the Codex image model (GPT Image, gpt-5.6-terra)
> using your own ChatGPT login, and exposes it over the Model Context Protocol
> (MCP). It runs as a hosted multi-user service and as a local stdio server.

- Source: https://github.com/giulianoo0/pintr
- Hosted service: https://pintr.giuli.dev
- MCP endpoint: https://pintr.giuli.dev/mcp
- License / contributing: see the repo (LLM contributions welcome, human-reviewed)

pintr never asks for an API key. You sign in with a ChatGPT account through
OAuth; the driver model is fixed server-side (gpt-5.6-terra) so callers cannot
pass a different or bogus model.

Two modes:

- **Hosted (HTTP, multi-user):** users register (email + password), link one or
  more ChatGPT accounts from a dashboard, and connect MCP clients via the
  standard MCP OAuth flow. Generated images and reference uploads are encrypted
  at rest in S3-compatible storage (Cloudflare R2). This is https://pintr.giuli.dev.
- **Local (stdio, single user):** the client starts the pintr binary; it logs in
  with a local browser flow and saves tokens to `~/.config/pintr/auth.json`.
  Generated images are written to a pintr-chosen cache path returned as `saved_path`.

# Usage

## Connecting a client (hosted)

pintr speaks streamable HTTP MCP at `https://pintr.giuli.dev/mcp`. Two auth
methods are accepted on `/mcp`:

1. **MCP OAuth (recommended):** point the client at the URL. On first use it
   gets a 401, discovers the OAuth endpoints, and opens your browser; you log
   in to pintr and click allow, and the client keeps its own auto-refreshed
   token.
2. **Personal access key:** create one on the dashboard (shown once,
   `pintr_...`) and send it as a static header:
   `Authorization: Bearer pintr_YOURKEY`. It never expires until revoked.

Per-harness setup:

### Claude Code

```
claude mcp add --transport http pintr https://pintr.giuli.dev/mcp
```

With an access key instead of OAuth:

```
claude mcp add --transport http pintr https://pintr.giuli.dev/mcp \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer pintr_YOURKEY"
```

### OpenCode

`opencode mcp add` (interactive), or in `opencode.json`
(project or `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`):

```json
{
  "mcp": {
    "pintr": {
      "type": "remote",
      "url": "https://pintr.giuli.dev/mcp",
      "enabled": true
    }
  }
}
```

Add `"headers": {"Authorization": "Bearer pintr_YOURKEY"}` to use an access
key instead of OAuth.

### PI (pi coding agent)

In the MCP config (`.mcp.json` / pi settings):

```json
{
  "mcp": {
    "pintr": {
      "type": "remote",
      "url": "https://pintr.giuli.dev/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

Optional access key: `"headers": {"Authorization": "Bearer pintr_YOURKEY"}`.

### Codex CLI

```
codex mcp add pintr --url https://pintr.giuli.dev/mcp
```

Or in `~/.codex/config.toml`:

```toml
[mcp_servers.pintr]
url = "https://pintr.giuli.dev/mcp"
# optional access key instead of OAuth:
# bearer_token_env_var = "PINTR_KEY"   # export PINTR_KEY=pintr_YOURKEY
```

### Antigravity (CLI + IDE)

Shared config at `~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json` (note `serverUrl`, not
`url`):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "pintr": {
      "serverUrl": "https://pintr.giuli.dev/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

Optional access key: `"headers": {"Authorization": "Bearer pintr_YOURKEY"}`.

### Grok Build

Grok Build reads Claude-style MCP config (`.mcp.json` in the project):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "pintr": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://pintr.giuli.dev/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

For grok.com chat: grok.com/connectors → New Connector → Custom → paste the
URL and finish the auth flow.

### Anything else

Any MCP client with remote (streamable HTTP) support works: add a remote MCP
server pointing at `https://pintr.giuli.dev/mcp`. If the client can't run the
OAuth flow, pass `Authorization: Bearer pintr_YOURKEY` as a header. Plain
scripts/curl send the same header directly.

## MCP tools

### generate_image
Generate an image. Input:
- `prompt` (string, required) — the full image prompt.
- `reference_images` (string[], optional) — images to anchor a character or
  style. How to pass them depends on the mode:
  - **Local stdio server: pass LOCAL FILE PATHS.** The server runs on your
    machine and reads them directly off disk. This is local-only; hosted pintr
    cannot read a path from your computer.
  - **Hosted Claude.ai / Claude Desktop:** pass the `ref_` token returned by
    `request_reference_upload`. Tokens expire after one hour and can be reused
    until then.
- `reference_image_files` (optional, hosted ChatGPT only) — ChatGPT supplies
  attached images here automatically. Attach the image to the conversation and
  call `generate_image`; never manually construct file descriptors.

### hosted reference-image flows

- **ChatGPT:** attach an image to the conversation and call `generate_image`.
  The host fills `reference_image_files`; callers do not supply file metadata.
- **Claude.ai / Claude Desktop:** attach the image, then call
  `request_reference_upload` with its metadata. Claude's code-execution sandbox
  receives a signed URL and `PUT`s the attachment bytes to pintr over HTTPS.
  Once, add `https://pintr.giuli.dev` under **Settings → Capabilities → Code
  execution and file creation → Additional allowed domains** so the sandbox can
  reach pintr. The URL expires after five minutes; its response contains a
  `ref_` token, which Claude passes to `generate_image.reference_images` for up
  to one hour. The image bytes go from the sandbox to pintr over HTTPS, never
  through model-authored JSON.
- **Local stdio:** local file paths in `reference_images` work only because the
  server runs on the same machine. They are not a hosted workflow.

Do not embed image bytes, base64, or data URLs in a hosted tool call.

Generation can take up to 420 seconds — a long-running call is not stuck.
The server streams MCP progress notifications while it works and errors out
after 10 minutes.

Result (hosted): `asset_url` (presigned ciphertext), `decrypted_asset_url` (open
in a browser to view the decrypted PNG), `decryption_key`, `mime_type`, `model`,
`account`, `duration_ms`, `size_bytes`, and `usage` (the account's remaining
rate limits). Always open `decrypted_asset_url` to view the result. Stored
images are permanently deleted from storage 24 hours after generation —
download the PNG if you need it longer.
Result (stdio): `saved_path` plus the same metadata.

### get_usage
Return the remaining Codex rate limits for the linked account(s): the 5h, weekly
and monthly windows (only the ones OpenAI currently exposes), each with used and
remaining percent. Result: `{ "accounts": [ { account, plan_type, windows:[{label, used_percent, remaining_percent, resets_at}] } ] }`.

## HTTP endpoints

MCP + OAuth (RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata, RFC 8414 AS metadata, RFC
7591 dynamic client registration, authorization-code + PKCE, RFC 8707 audience):

- `POST /mcp` — MCP streamable HTTP endpoint (bearer required; OAuth access token
  or `pintr_...` access key). Returns 401 with `WWW-Authenticate` when unauthed.
- `GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` (and `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp`) — resource metadata.
- `GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` — authorization server metadata.
- `POST /register` — dynamic client registration.
- `GET|POST /authorize` — authorization endpoint (requires a logged-in session; shows a consent page).
- `POST /token` — token endpoint (authorization_code and refresh_token grants).

Assets (all content encrypted at rest; keys are returned once and never stored):

- `request_reference_upload` issues the short-lived, signed HTTPS destination
  used by Claude's code-execution sandbox. It is an MCP tool flow, not a
  bearer-authenticated upload API. Signed upload URLs expire after five minutes;
  the returned `ref_` token is reusable for one hour.
- `GET /view?o=<objectKey>&k=<key>` — fetches a stored ciphertext, decrypts it
  server-side, and returns the raw image (`image/png`). This is what
  `decrypted_asset_url` points to.

Dashboard (browser, session cookie + CSRF; signup/login and the linking/consent
forms may additionally require a Cloudflare Turnstile check when the operator
enables it):

- `GET /` — landing (redirects to /dashboard when signed in).
- `GET|POST /signup` — create an account (no key is minted at signup).
- `GET|POST /login`, `POST /logout` — session auth.
- `GET /dashboard` — manage linked ChatGPT accounts (with rate-limit bars),
  access keys, stored assets, and account deletion.
- `POST /link/start`, `POST /link/finish` — link a ChatGPT account (browser paste flow).
- `POST /accounts/default`, `POST /accounts/remove` — manage linked accounts.
- `POST /keys/create`, `POST /keys/remove` — personal access keys.
- `POST /tokens/revoke` — invalidate all issued OAuth tokens (per-user kill switch).
- `POST /assets/purge` — delete the user's stored objects; the `kind` field
  picks `generated` images, reference `uploads`, or (default) both.
- `POST /account/delete` — permanently delete the account and everything it owns
  (linked accounts, keys, sessions, and all stored objects in S3).
- `GET /llms.txt` — this document.

## Encryption, retention & privacy

- ChatGPT tokens are stored encrypted at rest (AES-256-GCM, key derived from the
  server secret which lives only in the environment). Passwords use argon2id.
- Each generated image and each reference upload is encrypted under a *fresh
  random AES-256-GCM key*. Only ciphertext is stored; the key is returned once in
  the response (or embedded in the upload handle) and never persisted. The bucket
  and pintr itself only ever hold ciphertext they cannot read.
- Retention: a background janitor permanently deletes expired objects from the
  bucket — reference uploads 1 hour after upload, generated images 24 hours
  after generation (matching the presigned URL lifetime). The dashboard keeps
  separate generated-image and reference-upload counts and can purge either or
  both immediately.
- The encryption protects data at rest (bucket operator, backups, a stolen DB),
  not against a compromised pintr process — pintr necessarily sees each image in
  memory at creation time.
- Optional anonymous analytics (Plausible): when enabled by the operator, the
  server counts events like signups and generations. An event is only a name —
  no user id, IP, prompt, or image data is ever sent. The hosted instance at
  pintr.giuli.dev has this enabled.

# Self-hosting

## Local stdio server (single user)

Build and point your MCP client at the binary (stdio transport):

```
go build -o pintr ./cmd/pintr
./pintr login          # optional: browser login up front
./pintr                # serve MCP over stdio (logs in first if needed)
```

Tokens are saved to `~/.config/pintr/auth.json` (0600). Reference images are
local file paths; results are written to a pintr-chosen cache path
(`saved_path`).

## Hosted server (multi user)

Environment (see `.env.example`):

- `PINTR_PUBLIC_URL` — public https base clients reach.
- `PINTR_DB` — SQLite path.
- `PINTR_SECRET` — >= 32 random chars; signs tokens and encrypts stored
  credentials. Keep it stable: rotating it makes every stored ChatGPT token
  undecryptable (users must re-link).
- `PINTR_S3_*` — `PINTR_S3_ENDPOINT`, `PINTR_S3_BUCKET`,
  `PINTR_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `PINTR_S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `PINTR_S3_REGION`,
  and optional `PINTR_S3_PUBLIC_BASE` for a bucket-bound custom domain.
  Without these the server runs but image generation is disabled.
- `PINTR_PLAUSIBLE_DOMAIN` / `PINTR_PLAUSIBLE_SCRIPT` — optional anonymous
  analytics (see above); both unset = fully off.
- `PINTR_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY` / `PINTR_TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY` — optional
  Cloudflare Turnstile on signup/login and the linking/consent forms,
  validated server-side; both unset = no captcha anywhere.

Run `pintr -http 127.0.0.1:8090` behind an HTTPS reverse proxy with response
buffering off (generations stream progress for minutes).
